title: Overview
text: Unprompted is a local-first prototype. It watches sources you authorize, notices work that was not assigned as a prompt, checks the evidence, and prepares the next step. You review the result. External actions stay behind an approval or a separate permission. This site matches the current main branch, version 0.3.0. It is for someone running the app, and for someone changing the code or calling the local API. What it does authorized source → observed change → evidence check → prepared work                   → your decision → external action, if permitted → readback Sources supply the work. A local folder needs no cloud account. Google, GitHub, Outlook, Slack, and Notion use your own account.

title: Install and first run
text: Requirements Node.js 20+ and npm. 22+ is recommended. The optional Pi harness needs 22.19+. Git, or a downloaded source archive opened in a terminal. A browser. A model endpoint, a model ID, and an API key when the provider requires one. A compatible local model can omit the key. A cloud account only if you connect that cloud source. A local folder needs no account. Apple Notes needs macOS. Check the runtime with node --version. Install and start git clone https://github.com/PStarH/unprompted.git cd unprompted npm ci --include=optional npm start npm ci --include=optional installs the pinned SQLite runtime and the optional Pi and MCP packages. title: Demo, and what it is not
Models
text: The model interprets requests and can correlate context. It cannot approve an action, grant a permission, or declare that work is complete. Connect from the app Run npm start, then enter: API endpoint model ID API key, if the provider requires one Verify and connect model sends one structured request using invented content. Only a successful check is saved. The key is stored in the private local setup file, not in workspace records, and it is not returned by the API or the event stream. Changing the endpoint does not reuse another provider's key. A saved connection uses primary interpretation. Rules can still recognize a request, and the model is still called. title: Connectors
text: Connectors let Unprompted read selected work and, when you allow it, use actions supported by the service. First connect a model, then open Connections. Start with one source; you do not need to connect everything. Sign in to your own accounts. An organization administrator may need to approve an app. Work sources and MCP A work source checks your selected content on connection and continues observing while the app runs, normally every five minutes. You can pause it or choose Check now. MCP supplies tools used during a task; it does not automatically poll for changes or create tasks. title: Workspace
text: The interface is a local page served by the app. It has English and Chinese strings. Nothing is sent to a project-hosted account. There is no login screen because the server is on localhost. Pages The sidebar has four destinations: Overview — the current tasks, a status line, and filters. Memory — preferences, rules, and experience you saved. You can edit, delete, or restore them. Connections — each source, its access, observation, search, work artifacts, and MCP. Settings — appearance, Your standing agreements, and Notifications & learning: quiet hours and how often the app may ask. Agreements and appearance do not grant a connector write. The rules are on Automatic follow-up. Task filters

title: How work moves
text: A change in a source you authorized is the trigger. You do not write a prompt for each item. event → request → evidence → prepared action → your decision       → external action, if permitted → readback The model can interpret and draft. Deterministic checks own identity, permissions, review tokens, dispatch, and verification. A model reply cannot approve an action or mark a task done. What a pass looks like A connector records a message, a file change, an issue, or a note. The app looks for a request and for evidence in the sources you allowed. Missing or stale evidence keeps the work open. It does not become a confident answer. A prepared reply or patch appears under To review, with the ev

title: Automatic follow-up
text: The default is still one approval at a time. Automatic follow-up is a lease you start yourself. It removes later clicks. It does not skip evidence, permissions, or a readback. Shadow mode hides these controls and refuses the request. An explicit UNPROMPTEDSHADOWMODE=true blocks external writes, and the connector still needs its own grant. See Permissions and privacy. Two different switches Send & allow future follow-ups is on a prepared reply. It sends this reply and records a standing agreement for that scope. Settings lists them under Your standing agreements. Ask me each time ends the agreement. It does not recall a reply already sent. Timed automatic follow-up is separate. Follow this au

title: Permissions and privacy
text: Reads start when you connect a source. Writes do not. The server binds to localhost and has no authentication. Do not publish it through a tunnel, reverse proxy, or public host. Defaults Sources start with reads. Platform actions need provider permission and a local account and API path grant; / covers all API paths for that platform. Dedicated Google send and Docs editing flows have their own action settings. See Google Workspace. General GitHub, Slack, Outlook, Notion, Google and Todoist API actions depend on actual provider permissions and the locally granted scope. Creating an Apple Note needs a folder grant. title: FAQ
text: These answers match the current app. Each one links to the longer page. Does it run in the cloud? No. npm start binds to 127.0.0.1 on your machine. There is no login and no hosted workspace. Do not publish that port through a tunnel or reverse proxy. See Security. Do I need an Unprompted account? No. You connect your own model and authorize your own source accounts. A distribution can ship the connector apps already registered. You do not paste a client ID to get started. See Connectors. Will it send mail or edit documents on its own? A source starts read-only. title: Architecture
text: Unprompted is a Node.js process with SQLite, a browser interface in public/, and HTTP in server.js. better-sqlite3 is required. Pi Agent Core and the MCP client are optional. The demo keeps a JSON store. One piece of work event → normalize → request → correlate → evidence       → prepare → check authority → execute → verify A later event can reassess an open request. An unrelated event is stored without a task. If newer evidence invalidates a draft, the draft is withdrawn. Completion requires a verified result, not a model sentence. Modules Layer Role Where Connectors Read sources and keep cursors `src/connectors/` Context Requests, documents, freshness `src/requests.js`, `src/store.js` Plan

title: Glossary
text: Source A place the app is allowed to read. Local folders, Apple Notes, Google, GitHub, Outlook, Slack, and Notion are sources. Connecting one does not allow a write. Observation A read of a connected source. Connecting checks once, then repeats on the interval saved in Connections. The default is 5 minutes. The choices are 1 minute, 5 minutes, 15 minutes, and 1 hour. You can pause it, or choose Check now. The process has to stay running. An empty read can be a real result. This is polling, not a webhook. Evidence The source material a requirement is checked against. Missing or stale evidence keeps the work open. A model reply is not evidence by itself. title: Security
text: Unprompted is a pre-1.0 prototype. Fixes land on main. There is no separate supported release branch, no bounty, and no promised response time. Everyday permissions are on Permissions and privacy. This page is how to report a vulnerability, and what must stay out of a public issue. Report a vulnerability Use GitHub private vulnerability reporting. If that page is unavailable, contact the maintainer through a private method listed on their profile. Do not post exploit details, credentials, or private content in a public issue. If you cannot find a private channel, open a short issue that only asks for one, and leave the technical detail out.
